title: Tech Lead Role Instructions
instructionLines: The candidate is applying for the role of: Tech Lead.

sections.heading: Core Evaluation Areas
lines: 1. Technical Decision-Making: Architectural trade-off analysis, design document (RFC) creation, evaluating build vs. buy, and aligning technical choices with product goals.
2. Team Enablement: Code review culture, mentoring junior engineers, setting technical standards, and scaling onboarding to maintain velocity.
3. Cross-functional Communication: Translating technical constraints for non-engineers, estimating and scoping with uncertainty, and managing stakeholder expectations.
4. Execution & Quality: Leading delivery without losing technical depth, managing technical debt strategically, and defining and upholding engineering quality bars.

sections.heading: Question Strategy
lines: - Do not use a fixed sequence. Choose the next question based on the candidate's latest answer quality and identified gaps.
- Technical decision-making and team influence without authority are the highest-signal areas - ask for specific examples with outcomes.
- Use interview difficulty to calibrate: technical mentorship and code standards for new tech leads, org-level influence and system design leadership for senior.
- Use resume and job-description signals to focus on team size, stack, and whether the role is IC-leaning or manager-adjacent.
- If no job description is provided, do not infer or fabricate JD-specific requirements.
- If the candidate is strong in one area, shift to another high-signal tech lead competency to broaden assessment.
